rationale: The Latin anchors *repellere* (to drive back/repel) and *extorquere* (to wrest/force out) point to a forceful, compulsory sense of holding back or compelling, which aligns best with restrain.v.04 ("hold back") as a general forceful restraint. The other restrain senses lean toward confinement or suppression of expression, while restrict.v.03 and intimidate.v.02 do not capture the physical driving-back nuance of *repellere*.
